findings.reason: the plan's dispatch graph would not put the row-exchange case record and its route in the §4 node's brief, and a §4 node would discover the missing input after it had started.
findings.text: §4 reads the inverse baseline's row-exchange case, its record (`docs/evidence/fragments/inverse-equilibrium-baseline/efit-on-nova-rows.html`) and the solver route that section used, but its declared dependency list is empty (`"s4":[]`) and its prose says only "waits on nothing in this plan"; every other section in the plan that reads another plan's landed section declares the edge (`s1` → `inverse-equilibrium-baseline#s2`), and the inverse plan declares the reverse edge (`docs/plans/inverse-equilibrium-baseline.html:24`, `s4` → `forward-solve-near-stored-states#s4`), so the graph is asymmetric at the one place §4's inputs come from

findings.reason: the verdict is the plan's only gate on §3's scope, so an unqualified verdict can park a case for reasons that belong to the measurement rather than to the case.
findings.text: §2(1) commits the Reached/Not-reached verdict (which decides whether §3 owes a case a repair, and which the plan permits to park a case permanently) to a chained sequence of seven solves at 1e-10, but §2 names no device, mesh or solver route for those solves while §1(1) names the H200/titan batch and §3(1) names the H200 for the endpoint it must reach; convergence at a fixed tolerance is a device- and mesh-qualified measurement in this repository (the forward gate guidance requires the device to be stated, and a titan or CPU number is not an H200 number), so a case can be marked Not reached on one device and be reachable on the device §3 is held to

findings.reason: a citation a later reader cannot open is not evidence, and the batching section's stated root cause (tracer-array conversion under the batched Newton-Krylov call) is checkable only through that receipt.
findings.text: the two route-inventory receipts that carry §4's cited refusal are given as `~/.cache/nova-inverse-equilibrium-baseline/route-inventory-cpu.json` and a bare `route-inventory-titan.json` with no directory; a HOME-relative receipt does not resolve for a reader whose HOME is remapped, which is how this crew runs (measured in this run: `ls ~/.cache/nova-inverse-equilibrium-baseline` exits nonzero because HOME resolved to the run's own `omp-home`, while `/home/ITER/mcintos/.cache/nova-inverse-equilibrium-baseline/route-inventory-cpu.json` exists, 3248 bytes), and the project rule puts receipts that make evidence claims on the GPFS evidence root with the resolved path recorded

findings.reason: the section's single property is that a batch runs; requiring every displaced copy to converge makes that property unmeasurable whenever the pre-existing convergence defect fires, and the node would spend its gate on §3's subject instead.
findings.text: §4(1) requires 16 and then 64 independently displaced copies (each a 1 % change in profile amplitudes) of the nova-written ITER state to *every one qualify below 1e-10* in one traced programmed batch, and §4 declares it waits on nothing, so no repair of displaced solves may be assumed: the positive control the section added covers only the undisplaced generating state solved alone at the reference mesh (residual 1.17e-15, `docs/evidence/fragments/inverse-equilibrium-baseline/efit-on-nova-rows.html`), and the plan's own evidence is that displacing profile coefficients breaks qualification (the MAST-U first perturbed solve stalls at 1.2e-4 with the active-set step refused, §1(1)), which is exactly the class of failure §3 exists to repair; the batched arm can therefore fail on displaced-state convergence rather than on batching, and its negative control (base revision does not return per-state flags) cannot tell the two apart
